claim: Two things. (A) Whether the judge's 'yours' minus profiled kernel time (≈0 for r6's zero-smem gv kernels, +2.5-3.5 µs for ours at m=1, +1.5-4.9 for nvjet, +6.8 for the FP32 xmma) is an L1/shared-memory carveout reconfiguration at launch. The flush kernel (torch.sum) runs with little or no shared memory, so a following kernel that opts into a large dynamic smem forces the SM to re-partition L1/smem first. The carve probes measure that directly, with no memory traffic (empty kernels) and on a stream (bulk ring sizes, unused smem on a ring kernel, our own flush with and without smem). (B) pw5 showed the last-arriver finalize (ld.cg read-back from L2) is the bulk of the epilogue (3.8 of 5.8 µs at m=32). pw6 removes the global workspace entirely on the m<=32 paths. The K-split CTAs of one n-block form a cluster, park their partials in their own drained W-ring smem, and after one cluster barrier each rank sums its own row-tile slice from all peers over DSMEM and stores bf16. A second cluster barrier keeps peers' smem alive. There are no global reductions, fences, counters, finalize or zeroing. Predicted pooler m=32 epilogue: ~1 µs (one cluster barrier pair + 32 KB of DSMEM reads per CTA) instead of 5.8, i.e. the full path near pw4's noepi + ~1.5.
target_shapes: pooler m=32: pw-b16t4c below pw-b16t4g by >= 3 µs within the run (pw4: b16t4 26.4 in-prepare)
pooler m=1/8/16 and qkv m=1..32: c below g by 1-2 µs; qkv only has 9 n-blocks, so its clusters of 8 give 72 CTAs (bandwidth-short, the bake-off decides)
unpooler n=1024: pw-b8t1c (64 CTAs) vs pw-b8t1 (pw4's winner there)
m=128: tm / tms unchanged from pw4
kill_if: Kill the cluster epilogue if pw-b16t4c is not at least 2 µs below pw-b16t4g on pooler m=32 within the run, or if any c path declines with -9 (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters == 0) on the H200 at these smem sizes. If the carve lines show the carveout hypothesis (smem-dependent launch cost of 1.5 µs or more), the next design must hold dynamic smem near the flush kernel's configuration or move to a zero-smem engine. If they show the null, the yours-minus-kernel gap is elsewhere (graph/launch overhead per kernel node) and must be looked for in the replay structure.

probe_plan.where: prepare(), after compile and before the bake-off, <= 15 s, try/except, selects nothing. 'PROBE carve <name> <us>'. Timing is the harness's _time_us (256 MB torch.sum flush before every replay, median of 15) except the two own-flush lines, which use _time_us_flush (identical, with a custom flush callable; the harness's _time_us is unchanged). 15 lines.

lines.empty 132x256 smem=0K / 64K / 200K: An empty kernel (one word per CTA) with that much dynamic smem opted in. Carveout hypothesis: 0K ≈ the replay floor (~4.8), 64K and 200K higher by the reconfiguration cost (~1.5-3 µs, growing with the size switched to). Null: all three equal within ~0.2 µs.
lines.empty 132x256 smem=200K x2: Two such launches back to back in one graph. Hypothesis, per-switch cost: ≈ the 200K line + one launch gap (~1 µs), because the second launch finds the carveout already set. Per-launch cost: ≈ 2x the 200K delta. Null: floor + one launch gap.
lines.bulk ring=8K/16K/32K/64K/100K/160K: pw2's pure bulk stream (1 consumer warp, 132 CTAs, 50 MB) with total dynamic smem 4Kx2, 8Kx2, 16Kx2, 16Kx4, 25Kx4, 40Kx4. Hypothesis: time rises with the smem footprint (a step above the default carveout), since the stream itself was flat across 16-32 KB stages in pw2. Null: flat at the pure-stream time (~16.5-18.7 depending on judge drift); 8K/16K may be slightly slower from fewer bytes in flight.
lines.ring D=8 8w x 528 smem=0K / 48K: pw2's register-ring stream (8 warps x 4 CTAs/SM, no smem use) as is, then with 48 KB of unused dynamic smem per CTA. 48 rather than 64 KB: 4 x 64 KB would cut residency to 3 CTAs/SM and change more than the carveout. Hypothesis: 48K slower by the reconfiguration cost. Null: equal (the loads bypass L1, so a smaller L1 does not matter).
lines.bulk ring=64K flush=torch.sum / own-kern: The 64K bulk stream after three flushes: torch.sum (the harness), our own 256 MB read kernel with 200 KB dynamic smem (132 x 1024 threads), and the same kernel with 0 smem. Hypothesis: the 200K-flush line is faster than the other two by the reconfiguration cost, because the carveout is already large when our kernel starts. Null: all three equal.

probe_plan.reading: Compare lines within this run only (the judge drifts about 10% between runs). The empty-kernel lines isolate launch configuration from memory traffic; the flush lines test the mechanism directly.

cluster_design.grid: (NB, KS) with one BN=256 n-block per CTA, launched with cudaLaunchKernelEx and cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension (1, KS, 1), so a cluster is the KS K-split CTAs of one n-block and cluster_ctarank = blockIdx.y. KS = the largest of {8, 4, 2, 1} with NB*KS <= 132, KS <= K/64 and dividing the 16 row tiles, whose x slice + W ring fits. Grids: pooler 16x8 = 128, qkv 9x8 = 72, o 32x4 = 128, unpooler (m>=16) 32x4 = 128, unpooler n=1024 4x8 = 32 (b16) / 8x8 = 64 (b8t1c). smem 100-161 KB, 1 CTA/SM.
cluster_design.epilogue: After the K loop the producer warp does not exit; it joins a CTA-wide __syncthreads. At that point every consumer has passed its last full-barrier wait, so every W bulk copy has landed and been read, and the producer has issued its last stage. The W ring area is then free. The consumers store their fp32 accumulators (fragment order, all lanes; 8 KB at m<=8, 16 KB at m=16, 32 KB at m=32; ring >= 96 KB) at sbase + idx*16 with st.shared.v4. Then barrier.cluster.arrive.release + wait.acquire. Rank r owns fragments [r*FRAG/KS, (r+1)*FRAG/KS), which are row tiles [r*16/KS, (r+1)*16/KS) because fragments are tile-major. All 544 threads take an index each; for valid tokens (tok < m) they issue all KS mapa.shared::cluster + ld.shared::cluster.v4.f32 loads (peers 0..KS-1) before the adds, then store bf16. Finally a second cluster arrive/wait so no CTA exits while a peer still reads its smem. KS == 1: direct bf16 store from registers, no cluster launch.
cluster_design.launch_guard: The launcher checks NG == NB, KS <= 8, KS | 16 and staging <= ring bytes. It calls cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters once per (KS, smem), caching up to 8 entries so graph capture does not repeat it, and returns -9 when it reports 0 or fails. cudaLaunchKernelEx errors are returned as codes. Any code makes run() use the fallback, so a cluster that cannot be placed declines instead of failing.
cluster_design.kept_for_comparison: pw-b16t1g / b16t2g / b16t4g: pw4's global red.v4 + counter + last-arriver epilogue, same kernel body (CLU = 0), registered in the same run. pw-b8t1 (global) and pw-b8t1c (cluster) both serve unpooler n=1024 only.
cluster_design.registers_ptxas: nvcc 12.8 sm_90a -O3, all 0 stack / 0 spill: b16t1c 62, b16t2c 64, b16t4c 85, b8t1c 62, b16t1g 60, b16t2g 66, b16t4g 92, b8t1 65, tm 150; probes pw_probe_bulk 22, pw_probe_ring8 48, pw_probe_flush 16, pw_probe_empty2 10, pw_probe_empty 10.

paths: pw-b16t1g, pw-b16t1c (m 1, 8); pw-b16t2g, pw-b16t2c (m 16); pw-b16t4g, pw-b16t4c (m 32), all four BF16 layers. pw-b8t1, pw-b8t1c (unpooler n=1024, m 1, 8). pw-tm, pw-tms (m 128). Router, m=256 and odd m stay on the fallback.
compile_check: 14/14 kernels with 0 stack and 0 spill (above). The full CUDA_SRC, including the cudaLaunchKernelEx cluster launch and cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters, compiles with -std=c++20 against the minimal torch mock with no errors or warnings.
verification_done_offline: emu_pw6.py (scratchpad). (1) The pw2 emulator with pw6's CLU data path: per-CTA staging in fragment order, rank-owned slices summed over peers 0..KS-1 in kernel order, bf16 store for tok < m. It asserts that the rank slices partition the n-block, that each slice is whole row tiles, and that no unwritten staging slot is read. b16t1c (KS 8, 2 clusters), b16t4c (KS 4, odd m=27), b16t2c (KS 2), b16t4c (KS 1, direct) and b8t1c (KS 8, one row tile per rank) are bit-exact on one-hot rows and fp64-exact on random rows. (2) 450 randomized interleavings of KS = 2/4/8 CTAs (ring depth 2/4, 1-16 stages): W ring, CTA barrier, staging writes, cluster barrier 1, peer reads, cluster barrier 2, exit. No deadlock, no staging write while a bulk copy is in flight, no peer read before write or after exit. Dropping cluster barrier 2 is caught 30/30; dropping the consumers-drained condition of the CTA barrier 25/30. Lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9.
risks: Cluster scheduling: a cluster of 8 CTAs at 1 CTA/SM and 112-161 KB smem must be co-scheduled within a GPC. H200 GPCs hold 16-18 SMs, so two clusters of 8 per GPC fit, but placement can leave SMs idle (pooler 128 CTAs on 132 SMs). If occupancy reports 0 the path declines (-9). If it launches but packs badly, the c lines are slower than g and the bake-off keeps g.
qkv (9 n-blocks) only reaches 72 CTAs with clusters of 8; expect qkv to stay on g or torch.
The DSMEM reads are latency-bound (KS loads per fragment, 0.5-4 fragments per thread). If the cluster barrier itself is slow (the probes cannot isolate it), c may only tie g at m=1.
Log: 15 PROBE lines + about 40 PW build + about 150 BAKE/PICK lines, about 9 KB. Prepare: 10 paths; m=1 validation for 4 paths (2 b16 x 4 layers + 2 b8t1 x 1 layer), about 12 s.
